result.title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
result.summary: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. Drawing on the practice of human animators, we introduce DyCraft, a system for animated 3D scene generation that breaks animation into steps that coding agents can more reliably solve. DyCraft first expands the user's prompt into a detailed plan and builds a static scene. It then creates a 3D storyboard of key animation poses, where each frame is a static 3D scene that the agent can build and debug in isolation. Storyboarding decomposes the problem into pairs of verified start and end states, allowing the agent to author local motion between them with a collection of motion authoring tools. We evaluate DyCraft on 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks covering humanoid robots, human and animal characters, and physical mechanisms. Compared with a native GPT-6 agent in Codex and prior agentic baselines, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations and generates higher-quality animated 3D scenes that are more often preferred by human raters.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DyCraft，将长时程 3D 动画生成拆成提示词规划、静态场景搭建与关键姿态 3D 分镜三步，让编码智能体在已验证的起止状态之间编写局部运动，并在 24 个长时程多镜头任务上对比基线评估物理合理性与人类偏好。
AI.relevance_reason: 用可独立搭建和调试的分镜帧作为已验证中间状态来分解长程生成，可供核查其与长程推理中状态锚定、分段验证及停止决策的类比，但本身属 3D 动画生成，与 VLM latent 推理无直接联系。
